title: test(runtime): pin which sys_metadata row the /automation flow doors write; no caller holds a package to name
body:
Fixes #23292
Clause-②: no

## What this is

The card asks that `registerAndSaveFlow` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`) name the package of the flow it registers whenever its caller has one, and that a pin hold the two-package case either way. The `plugin-security` half of the card is gone from `main` (`permission-set-projection.ts` deleted by `dac99c2277`, `position-write-through.ts` with `storedRowPackageArg` by `5c9bfb0d3f`), so this PR is the runtime half only.

Measured on `main`: **none of the door's three callers holds a package**, so the save keeps naming none. This PR ships the pins the card asks for, over a real store, and records the measured reason on the function so the next reader does not thread a guessed package into the save. **No runtime behaviour changes.** This is the dispatch's mechanism (b), reported here as a deviation from its suggested route (thread an optional `packageId`): there is no source to thread from.

## The measurement

Real store (better-sqlite3, the real `ObjectQL` engine, the real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`), every request through `HttpDispatcher.dispatch()`. Packages `com.qa.alpha` and `com.qa.beta` are installed writable bases.

**What package a row this door writes can carry.** The protocol resolves a save that names no package (ADR-0048): the one package's row when the flow's active rows are bound to exactly one, else the package-unbound row.

- A flow saved into alpha through `/meta`, then `PUT /automation/solo_flow`: `200`, rows `[com.qa.alpha]`, label updated, no package-unbound row minted.
- `POST /automation` of a new flow: `200`, rows `[null]` (the package-unbound row).

**How a name comes to be held by two packages.** `PUT /meta/flow/shared_flow?package=com.qa.alpha`, then `?package=com.qa.beta`: both `200`, one active row per package. The automation door itself cannot mint a second package's row, because it never names a package.

**What each call site holds.**

- `POST /` and `PUT /:name` take a definition and a path. The only package-shaped value either reaches is a `_packageId` stamp, from one of two places:
  - **On the caller's body.** These are the caller's bytes. Reading them as the write address would make the body a package selector this door never declared, which is a widening the dispatch rules out.
  - **On the definition the engine holds.** For a two-package name, the protocol's execution view (`getMetaItemsForExecution`, which the boot bind arms from) lists both rows as contenders. `resolveFlowPrecedence` ties two runtime contenders and keeps arrival order. Measured: seeded alpha then beta, the view lists beta first and the engine holds `_packageId: com.qa.beta`; seeded beta then alpha, it lists alpha first. So the held stamp is a driver-order pick. That is the guess the 409 refuses to make, not a package the caller holds.
- `POST /:name/clone` writes a **new** name. `cloneFlowDefinition` drops the protection envelope, `_packageId` included (`FLOW_CLONE_DROPPED_KEYS`, ADR-0126 §7.1). The source's package is not the target's.
- `HttpProtocolContext` carries no package.

## What changes

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-flow-door-package-address.test.ts` (new, 12 pins):
  - A flow one package holds: `PUT /:name` saves to that package's row only, with no package-unbound row minted.
  - A flow no package holds: `POST /` saves the package-unbound row.
  - A flow two packages hold, in **both** seed orders, so whichever contender the engine holds:
    - The state is reachable through the `/meta` door, and the engine holds one contender's stamp.
    - `PUT /:name`, `POST /` onto the held name, `POST /` while the engine holds none, and `POST /:name/clone` onto the name each answer `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`.
    - Both rows are deep-equal before and after, and no third row is minted.
    - The engine is put back: the definition it held is re-registered (the same object), or the new name is withdrawn.
  - Refusals assert `code` + `status` and the rows read back from the store. No refusal prose is pinned.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`: one bullet in `registerAndSaveFlow`'s doc comment. It states why no package is named and what a two-package name answers, and that neither stamp is to be passed as `packageId`. Comment only.

## Evidence

On the merged head `6c0c016164` (`main` `873151021f` merged in):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --reporter=verbose src/domains/automation-flow-door-package-address.test.ts`: `Tests 12 passed (12)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0, `check:test-typecheck: OK`, 190 errors and 68 signatures held. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new file, and it has 0 errors.
- Full runtime `local` project, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`, on the merged head: `Test Files 379 passed (379)`, `Tests 5553 passed | 19 skipped (5572)`. Before the merge, at `1b04501693`, it was 377 files and 5499 tests passed.
- **Mutation proofs** (one-shot, through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode). The subject resolves through `src`, by the relative import of `../http-dispatcher.js`, so no `dist` leg is needed.
  - **Mutation 1, the forbidden route:** pass the engine-held `_packageId` to `saveMetaItem`. 4 failed, 8 passed. The four are `PUT /:name` and `POST /` onto the held name in both seed orders, each answering `200` where `409` was pinned. Restored: the blob equals HEAD (`0684fb34d327`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
  - **Mutation 2:** delete `restoreFlowRegistration(...)` from the refused-save branch. 8 failed, 4 passed: every two-package refusal pin in both orders. Restored the same way. The first attempt at this mutation used a replacement that was a substring of its anchor, and the tool refused it before any test ran. It was re-run with `--delete`.
- Lint: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the 2 changed files: exit 0, 2 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings. These are the flags `pnpm lint` uses; the repo-wide scan is CI's.
- Derived gate families: 53 commands from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, with the `--ran` reconciliation in the seat report. On the first run, `check:query-options-erasure` went red on one test-surface options cast (236 to 237). It was fixed in `cdbed1bf31` by removing the cast and re-ran green. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET (no whole-repo build), so it is NOT MEASURED locally, and its reading is CI's.

## Changeset: none, `skip-changeset`

Nothing publishes. The `src` change is a comment, and the new file is a test. To measure it, `@objectstack/runtime` was built and every `dist` file in its `files[]` was searched:

- A phrase from the new bullet appears 0 times in `index.js`, `index.cjs`, both maps and both `.d.ts`.
- Positive control: the `automation.ts` string literal `Flow definition body required` appears 2 times in `index.js` and 2 in `index.cjs`.
- The function's pre-existing doc comment is absent from `dist` too, so esbuild drops it.

The dispatch named a `patch` changeset, premised on a fix. With no behaviour change, the repo's rule is the `skip-changeset` label.

## Acceptance notes

- **The removal half, read and not changed.** `DELETE /automation/shared_flow` on a two-package name answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, both rows remain, and the engine re-registers the definition it held. `unregisterAndDeleteFlow` has the same shape as the save half: loud, and restored. Nothing in this PR touches it.
- **The relayed 409's remedy, at this door, read and not changed.** The refusal text is the protocol's: "on the REST door add ?package= with the package id". The automation door reads no query on `PUT /:name`, so `PUT /automation/shared_flow?package=com.qa.alpha` answers the identical 409. A caller following the remedy at this door loops; the save that works is `PUT /meta/flow/shared_flow?package=...`. This is reported to the seat as a finding.
